comment: Pinned, non-secret deployment tooling for the Amazon Linux 2023 aarch64
production host. This exists so a replacement host prepares itself to the
same specification instead of to whatever the package mirrors happen to
hold that day.
Every value here was taken from the VERIFIED live host baseline, not from a
sensible-looking default. A lock that disagrees with the running host is
worse than no lock: it makes a replacement host quietly different from the
one that was tested.
Nothing secret belongs here: no account id, no instance id, no token, no
credential, no private key, no environment value.

install_path_comment: The path the live host actually uses. /usr/libexec/docker/cli-plugins is
also on Docker's plugin search path, so installing there as well would
leave two plugins whose precedence depends on the Docker version -- and
an upgrade would then change the Compose in use without anything having

docker_compose.minimum_reason: compose.prod.yaml uses the !override tag, added in Compose 2.24.

comment: Compose v5 has no legacy builder to fall back to: `docker compose build`
refuses to run without buildx, with 'compose build requires buildx 0.17.0
or later'. The first install failed exactly there, having already passed
every other gate. Amazon Linux 2023's docker package does not supply a
buildx new enough, so it is pinned here like Compose rather than left to
whatever the mirrors hold.
The digest below was taken from the published checksums.txt AND confirmed
by hashing the downloaded asset independently.

linux_aarch64.asset_comment: docker/buildx names its aarch64 asset 'linux-arm64'; docker/compose names the same architecture 'linux-aarch64'.
install_path_comment: The same directory as the pinned Compose plugin. Docker searches
so a buildx shipped by the docker package is superseded without being

docker_buildx.minimum_reason: The floor Compose v5.3.1 itself enforces before it will build.

ssm_agent_reason: interpolationType: ENV_VAR on a document parameter. Older agents ignore
the declaration and fall back to raw string substitution of the parameter
into the command text -- which is exactly the behaviour the deployment
document is written to avoid. Verified in production: 3.3.4624.0.

comment: Approved Amazon Linux 2023 packages, checked with rpm -q and installed
only when missing. curl-minimal is deliberately listed rather than curl:
AL2023 ships curl-minimal, and installing full curl requires an erase of
curl-minimal, which is exactly the kind of unrelated churn a deployment
must not perform.
bootstrap_comment: The only packages the fixed SSM document may install itself, and only
when absent. Everything else is installed by the reviewed
ensure-host-prerequisites.sh inside the release being deployed.
packages.forbidden_reason: Installing full curl would erase curl-minimal.

expected_comment: The live host baseline. `local` rather than `json-file`: it is the driver
already in use, and changing a running host's log driver rewrites how
every container's logs are stored for no deployment-related reason.
systemd_mount_reason: Without it, Docker can start before the data volume is mounted and write
its entire image store to the root filesystem, which then fills.
rules: An existing file that disagrees is reported, never edited.
A `hosts` entry containing a TCP listener is a hard failure.
The radio account is never added to the docker group.
